metadata.disclaimer: Based on NIST's crosswalk from SP 800-53 Rev 5 to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (OLIR entry 155), with OSA's coverage estimates. Validate with qualified assessors for compliance or audit use.

crosswalk_check.source: NIST, SP 800-53 Rev 5 to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 crosswalk, v1.0.0 (OLIR entry 155, posted 2023-11-13)
crosswalk_check.scope: Base controls only, and every pair here is NIST's. The crosswalk pairs 533 base controls with clauses, all of them current, and all 533 pairs are here. A row that names an enhancement, such as CA-02(01) for A.5.35, counts for its base control, as in the HIPAA and NERC CIP mappings. Russell agreed that rule on 2026-11-01. Such rows add 25 pairs, listed under from_enhancements_only, so the mapping has 558. None of the enhancements NIST names is withdrawn. On 1 November 2026 OSA dropped the 240 pairs of its own that it had kept beside NIST's, because their source can't be confirmed, and 11 of them came back from enhancement rows. added_from_source lists the 313 pairs OSA took from the crosswalk in October 2026, and OSA already had the other 220. The coverage figures, rationales and gaps are OSA's. coverage_review lists the ones one rater adjusted after the rebuild.

coverage_review.status: adjusted by one rater after the rebuild
coverage_review.method: In the rebuild of 1 November 2026, 96 clauses lost controls and 14 regained some from enhancement rows. One rater set the figure of each, against the SP 800-53 statements of the controls it now has and of the enhancements NIST names. Each rationale names only those controls. No figure is above OSA's earlier figure for the clause or its twin. A figure went down where the dropped controls carried part of the clause, and a clause with no control left has 0. Each changed figure ends its rationale with the reason, and the gaps say what is uncovered where they no longer matched the figure. An Annex A control and its ISO/IEC 27002:2022 twin have the same controls and one figure. Six raters shared the first pass, on the clauses that lost controls, by group of clauses. A seventh rater then re-rated the clauses that regained controls and settled one figure for each pair of twins that differed. Each figure was set by one rater.

clauses.title: Understanding the organization and its context
clauses.rationale: PM-11 defines mission and business processes and the protection needs that come from them. PM-01's program plan gives an overview of the program's requirements. Clause 4.1 asks for a broader analysis of the organization's context, including external and internal issues beyond security risk. OSA lowered this figure from 70% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for risk context and critical infrastructure planning.
clauses.gaps: No direct SP 800-53 control for analyzing external/internal issues (political, economic, social factors) affecting ISMS. Organizational context determination is broader than security risk assessment.

clauses.title: Understanding the needs and expectations of interested parties
clauses.rationale: PM-01's program plan sets out the program's requirements and how organizational entities coordinate on them. Clause 4.2 asks the organization to identify every interested party and their requirements. OSA lowered this figure from 55% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for mission planning and supply chain relationships.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 lacks explicit requirement to identify all interested parties (regulators, customers, partners) and their specific ISMS expectations. Stakeholder mapping and requirements analysis not directly covered. Mission partners and suppliers, as interested parties, are outside the control mapped here.

clauses.title: Determining the scope of the ISMS
clauses.rationale: PM-01's program plan describes what the security program must meet and the controls it uses. PM-09 sets one risk management strategy for the whole organization. PM-28 records the assumptions, constraints and risk tolerance behind it. OSA lowered this figure from 70% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for authorization boundaries and enterprise architecture.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 defines system boundaries per authorization but doesn't explicitly require ISMS scope statement. Multi-system/enterprise scope determination differs from individual system authorization boundaries. System boundaries and the enterprise architecture are outside the controls mapped here.

clauses.title: Information security management system
clauses.rationale: PM-01 sets the program plan and keeps it reviewed and updated. PM-09 sets the risk management strategy, and PM-31 the continuous monitoring strategy that tracks how well controls work. PM-30 adds a strategy for supply chain risk. OSA lowered this figure from 78% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for program leadership and resources.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 doesn't use PDCA/process approach terminology. Continuous improvement cycle and ISMS as a formal management system with documented processes is implicit rather than explicit.

clauses.title: Leadership and commitment
clauses.rationale: PM-02 appoints a senior information security officer with the mission and resources to run the program. PM-29 appoints a senior official accountable for risk management and sets up a risk executive function. PM-03 puts security and privacy resources into capital planning. Clause 5.1 asks top management to show its commitment more directly. OSA lowered this figure from 72% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for management commitment and workforce development.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 doesn't explicitly require top management to demonstrate commitment through resource allocation, communication of importance, or ensuring ISMS achieves intended outcomes.

clauses.title: Policy
clauses.rationale: PL-01 directly requires security planning policy with management approval. PM-01 requires information security program plan. Policy establishment, approval, and communication well covered.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO specifies policy must be 'appropriate to the purpose of the organization' and 'available as documented information' with specific distribution requirements.

clauses.title: Organizational roles, responsibilities, and authorities
clauses.rationale: PM-02 assigns the lead information security role, and PM-29 the senior risk management roles. PM-01's program plan identifies and assigns roles and responsibilities. Each family's policy control, such as PL-01, PS-01 and AC-01, addresses roles and responsibilities for its area. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for security roles in position descriptions.
clauses.gaps: Minor gap. Plans and policies assign the roles here. Writing security roles into position descriptions is outside the controls mapped here.

clauses.title: Actions to address risks and opportunities
clauses.rationale: RA-03 covers risk assessment. PM-09 sets the risk management strategy, and PM-28 frames risk with its assumptions, constraints and risk tolerance. PM-04 tracks the remedial actions that respond to risk, and PM-06 measures performance. PM-01's program plan brings these together. OSA lowered this figure from 82% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for risk response and baseline selection.
clauses.gaps: ISO explicitly requires considering 'opportunities' alongside risks. SP 800-53 is risk-focused but doesn't explicitly address opportunities for improvement. Risk acceptance criteria less formalized.

clauses.title: Information security risk treatment
clauses.rationale: RA-07 responds to findings from assessments, monitoring and audits within the organization's risk tolerance. Its options of mitigating, accepting, sharing or avoiding a risk match ISO's risk treatment options. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for treatment plans and control selection.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires explicit Statement of Applicability (SoA) document. SP 800-53 doesn't have a direct SoA equivalent, though system security plans and baseline tailoring serve a similar purpose. The risk treatment plan, the choice of controls and the risk owners' approval are outside the control mapped here.

clauses.title: Information security objectives and planning to achieve them
clauses.rationale: PM-01 includes program objectives; PM-03 addresses resource planning; PM-06 covers security measures of performance. Objective-setting partially covered.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires measurable security objectives at relevant functions/levels with explicit plans (what, resources, responsible, completion, evaluation). SP 800-53 is less prescriptive about objective-setting methodology.

clauses.title: Planning of changes
clauses.rationale: NIST's crosswalk pairs no SP 800-53 control with this clause, so OSA maps none. OSA lowered this figure from 75% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for configuration change control and impact analysis.
clauses.gaps: ISO 6.3 is about planned changes to the ISMS itself (management system changes), not just technical changes. Organizational/process changes to the ISMS are not directly covered. OSA maps no control here, so the whole clause is a gap.

clauses.title: Resources
clauses.rationale: PM-03 directly addresses information security and privacy resources. It puts them into capital planning and investment requests and makes the planned resources available. OSA lowered this figure from 78% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for resources for systems and their development life cycle.
clauses.gaps: ISO requirement is broader - all resources needed for ISMS establishment, implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement. Budget allocation and resource planning less prescriptive in SP 800-53.

clauses.title: Competence
clauses.rationale: PM-13 sets up a workforce development program for security and privacy roles. It defines the knowledge and skills each role needs, provides role-based training and sets standards for measuring qualifications. OSA lowered this figure from 88% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for security training and training feedback.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires retaining documented evidence of competence, such as training records and certifications. Training for staff outside security and privacy roles, and the evaluation of training, are outside the control mapped here.

clauses.title: Awareness
clauses.rationale: AT-02 directly covers security awareness training, including awareness of policy, roles and responsibilities, and consequences. PS-08 sets a formal sanctions process for people who don't follow security policy. This aligns closely with the clause.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. AT-02 covers awareness of policy, contribution to ISMS effectiveness, and implications of non-conformance.

clauses.title: Communication
clauses.rationale: PM-01 disseminates the program plan across the organization. PM-31 reports security and privacy status to named roles at a set frequency, and PM-28 shares the results of risk framing. PM-15 keeps contact with security and privacy groups outside the organization.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires determining what, when, with whom, and how to communicate regarding ISMS. SP 800-53 lacks a systematic communication planning control. Internal/external communication strategy not explicitly required.

clauses.title: Documented information
clauses.rationale: PL-02 (system security plan) and PM-01 (program plan) address documentation, and each protects its plan from unauthorized disclosure and change. Each family's policy control, such as AC-01 and AU-01, documents policy and procedures and keeps them reviewed and updated. SA-05 adds system documentation, and CP-02 and IR-08 document the contingency and incident response plans. Documentation requirements are partially met. OSA lowered this figure from 75% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for audit records and their retention.
clauses.gaps: ISO has specific requirements for documented information control (creation, updating, version control, distribution, access, storage, disposal). SP 800-53 doesn't have a unified document management control.

clauses.title: Operational planning and control
clauses.rationale: PM-01 covers program implementation through the program plan. PL-07 describes how the organization intends to operate each system securely. CM-03 controls planned changes to systems. SA-01 and SA-04 set security requirements for acquired systems and services. OSA lowered this figure from 75% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for system security plans and control assessment.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires organizations to plan, implement, and control processes needed to meet requirements. Outsourced process control and documented evidence of process execution are gaps.

clauses.title: Information security risk assessment
clauses.rationale: RA-03 directly covers risk assessment at planned intervals or when significant changes occur, and documents the results. OSA lowered this figure from 92% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for vulnerability scanning and criticality analysis.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. RA-03 comprehensively covers risk assessment execution. ISO emphasizes retaining documented results.

clauses.title: Information security risk treatment
clauses.rationale: CA-05 (plan of action and milestones) addresses risk treatment plans, and PM-04 tracks those plans across the organization. RA-07 (Risk Response) explicitly addresses risk treatment with options for mitigation, acceptance, sharing or avoidance, closely aligning with ISO risk treatment concepts. OSA lowered this figure from 88% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for risk assessment.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO requires retaining documented results of risk treatment. POA&M process is close but doesn't perfectly map to ISO risk treatment plan format.

clauses.title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
clauses.rationale: CA-07 (continuous monitoring) and PM-06 (measures of performance) directly address monitoring and measurement. PM-31 sets the organization-wide metrics and how often controls are monitored and assessed. OSA lowered this figure from 82% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for system monitoring and testing plans.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires determining what to monitor, methods, when, who analyzes results. PM-06 is less prescriptive about evaluation methods and timing.

clauses.title: Internal audit
clauses.rationale: CA-02 covers control assessments, which work much like internal audits: it selects assessors, plans the scope and reports the results. CA-01 sets the assessment policy and procedures, and PM-31 sets how often controls are assessed. CA-07, through its enhancement CA-07(01) on independent assessment, has independent assessors monitor the controls on an ongoing basis.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires formal internal audit program with defined criteria, scope, frequency, methods, and auditor independence. CA-02 covers assessments but doesn't use audit terminology or require audit program management.

clauses.title: Management review
clauses.rationale: PM-01 requires periodic review of the program plan. CA-07 reports security and privacy status to named roles, and CA-06 has a senior official authorize each system. PM-29 gives senior leaders an accountable role in risk management. These partially address management review.
clauses.gaps: ISO specifies detailed management review inputs (audit results, stakeholder feedback, risk assessment changes, opportunities for improvement) and outputs (decisions, resource changes). SP 800-53 lacks formal management review structure.

clauses.title: Continual improvement
clauses.rationale: PM-31 sets organization-wide metrics and acts on what monitoring finds, which supports improvement. PM-01 and PM-09 keep the program plan and the risk management strategy reviewed and updated.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires explicit continual improvement processes for ISMS suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness. SP 800-53 supports continuous monitoring but doesn't explicitly require PDCA-style continual improvement methodology.

clauses.title: Nonconformity and corrective action
clauses.rationale: CA-05 (POA&M) addresses remediation of identified weaknesses. PM-04 tracks remediation plans. RA-07 (Risk Response) addresses responding to findings from assessments and audits, aligning with corrective action requirements.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires formal nonconformity management including root cause analysis, corrective action implementation, and effectiveness review. POA&M process is close but lacks formal nonconformity management structure.

clauses.title: Policies for information security
clauses.rationale: SP 800-53 has a policy and procedures control (-01) in each family, and nearly all of them are mapped here. PL-01 is the overarching planning policy, and PM-01 establishes the program plan. SR-01, new in Rev 5, adds supply chain policy to a comprehensive policy framework.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 policy requirements are more granular (per-family) while ISO expects a coherent policy set.

clauses.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
clauses.rationale: PM-02 directly assigns senior information security role. PS-01 covers personnel security roles. PS-09 (Position Descriptions) explicitly requires incorporating security and privacy roles into organizational position descriptions, strengthening role definition coverage. OSA lowered this figure from 92% on 1 November 2026, when it set one figure for this control and its twin in ISO/IEC 27002:2022, which has the same controls.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. With PS-09, ISO's requirement for defined security roles and responsibilities is comprehensively addressed.

clauses.title: Segregation of duties
clauses.rationale: AC-05 directly addresses separation of duties. Comprehensive coverage. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it set one figure for this control and its twin in ISO/IEC 27002:2022, which has the same controls.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Management responsibilities
clauses.rationale: PS-01 sets personnel security policy. PL-04 has each person acknowledge the rules of behavior before getting access, and PS-06 has them sign access agreements. PS-07 requires external providers to follow the organization's personnel security policies. PM-01's program plan records management commitment and roles. OSA lowered this figure from 82% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for management and leadership roles.
clauses.gaps: ISO emphasizes management requiring personnel to apply security per policies. SP 800-53 is less explicit about management enforcement responsibility.

clauses.title: Contact with authorities
clauses.rationale: IR-06 covers incident reporting to authorities. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for contact with outside security groups.
clauses.gaps: ISO also asks for standing contact with authorities, beyond incident reporting. IR-06, the one control mapped here, covers incident reporting.

clauses.title: Contact with special interest groups
clauses.rationale: PM-15 directly covers contacts with security groups and associations. SI-05 receives security alerts and advisories from outside organizations. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for the threat awareness program and its information sharing.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Threat intelligence
clauses.rationale: PM-16 sets up a threat awareness program that shares threat intelligence across organizations. RA-10 (Threat Hunting) adds proactive cyber threat hunting to search for indicators of compromise and detect advanced threats. OSA lowered this figure from 92% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for security advisories and threat identification in risk assessment.
clauses.gaps: RA-10 adds proactive threat hunting. Gathering advisories, and using threat intelligence in risk assessment, are outside the controls mapped here.

clauses.title: Information security in project management
clauses.rationale: SA-03 covers security in the system development life cycle, and SA-04 sets security requirements for acquisitions. PL-08 adds the security architecture, and SA-15 the development process and standards.
clauses.gaps: ISO specifically requires security in ALL project management regardless of project type. SA controls focus on system/software projects specifically.

clauses.title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
clauses.rationale: CM-08 directly covers the inventory of system components, at the detail needed for tracking, and keeps it reviewed and updated. OSA lowered this figure from 92% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for the system inventory and the location of information.
clauses.gaps: ISO includes 'associated assets' beyond information and system components. An inventory of the information itself, and of where it is held, is outside the control mapped here.

clauses.title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
clauses.rationale: PL-04 directly covers rules of behavior and acceptable use. MP-02, MP-04, MP-05, MP-06 and MP-07 set rules for media access, storage, transport, sanitization and use. PE-16 and PE-20 control and track assets as they move. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for the use of external systems.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Return of assets
clauses.rationale: PS-04 covers personnel termination including return of organizational assets.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Classification of information
clauses.rationale: RA-02 covers security categorization of information and systems. Well aligned.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO uses classification levels; SP 800-53 uses FIPS 199 categorization. Conceptually similar but terminology/methodology differs.

clauses.title: Labelling of information
clauses.rationale: MP-03 covers marking of media with distribution limits and handling caveats. PE-22 marks hardware components with the impact or classification level of the information they may handle. OSA lowered this figure from 88% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for security attributes on digital information and its categorization.
clauses.gaps: ISO covers labeling of all information forms. MP-03 and PE-22 mark media and hardware. Labels on digital information itself are outside the controls mapped here.

clauses.title: Information transfer
clauses.rationale: SC-07 boundary protection; SC-08 transmission confidentiality/integrity; AC-04 information flow enforcement; AC-20 external system use. CA-03 (Information Exchange) addresses information exchange agreements with external systems. AC-17, AC-18 and AC-19 cover remote, wireless and mobile connections, and PS-06 covers access agreements. OSA lowered this figure from 88% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for cryptographic key management.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO includes transfer agreements and policies for all forms (electronic, physical, verbal). SP 800-53 focuses on technical controls but CA-03 adds exchange agreements.

clauses.title: Access control
clauses.rationale: AC-01 sets the access control policy and procedures. AC-03 enforces approved authorizations in line with that policy, and AC-06 applies least privilege. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for account management and remote access.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 AC family is more detailed than ISO requirement.

clauses.title: Identity management
clauses.rationale: IA-02 and IA-08 identify and authenticate organizational and non-organizational users. IA-04 manages identifiers, and IA-05 manages authenticators. AC-02 manages accounts from creation to removal. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for identity proofing.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Authentication information
clauses.rationale: IA-05 directly covers authenticator management (passwords, tokens, etc.), including how people must protect their authenticators.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Access rights
clauses.rationale: AC-02 covers account management, including provisioning, review and revocation of access. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for least privilege.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Information security in supplier relationships
clauses.rationale: SR-01 sets the supply chain risk management policy and procedures. SR-02 adds a plan for managing supply chain risks across the life of a system, component or service, and keeps it up to date. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for acquisition contracts and the controls on suppliers and external service providers.
clauses.gaps: ISO emphasizes ongoing supplier relationship management and periodic review. The controls here set policy and a plan, so contract terms and the oversight of service providers fall outside this mapping.

clauses.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
clauses.rationale: SA-04 directly requires security requirements in acquisition contracts, including contracts for services. SR-03 covers supply chain controls and processes in agreements, and SR-05 adds contract tools and procurement methods.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO requires specific agreement terms for information protection. SA-04 is comprehensive but format differs.

clauses.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
clauses.rationale: SR-02 sets a supply chain risk management plan, and SR-03 the processes and controls that address weaknesses in the supply chain. SR-04 keeps the provenance of components, and SR-05 covers acquisition strategies. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for supplier assessments and checks that components are genuine.
clauses.gaps: The SR controls mapped here align well with ISO's supply chain requirements. Supplier assessments and checks that components are genuine fall outside this mapping.

clauses.title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
clauses.rationale: SA-09 includes ongoing monitoring of external service providers' control compliance. SR-06 covers supplier assessments and reviews.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires regular monitoring and review of supplier service delivery, change management of supplier services. SP 800-53 is less prescriptive about ongoing supplier service monitoring cadence.

clauses.title: Information security for use of cloud services
clauses.rationale: SA-09 covers external system services, including cloud services, with oversight roles and ongoing monitoring of providers. SA-04 puts security requirements and the split of responsibilities into the acquisition contract, and SR-05 adds acquisition strategies. SA-01 sets the system and services acquisition policy.
clauses.gaps: ISO 27001:2022 added cloud-specific control. SP 800-53 addresses cloud through general external service controls but lacks cloud-specific acquisition, use, management, and exit requirements. FedRAMP supplements this.

clauses.title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
clauses.rationale: IR-08 sets the incident response plan, which describes the response capability and names who is responsible for it. The organization distributes the plan to incident response staff and keeps it up to date. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for incident response procedures and the training and testing of responders.
clauses.gaps: Incident response procedures fall outside this mapping, along with the training and testing of responders.

clauses.title: Assessment and decision on information security events
clauses.rationale: IR-04 incident handling includes the detection and analysis of events. AU-06 reviews and analyzes audit records for unusual activity and reports what it finds. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for incident tracking and reporting.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Response to information security incidents
clauses.rationale: IR-04 comprehensively covers incident response, from containment and eradication through to recovery. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for incident reporting and response assistance.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Learning from information security incidents
clauses.rationale: IR-04 includes incident analysis and feeds lessons learned from incident handling into the response procedures and training. This addresses post-incident review.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO emphasizes using incident knowledge to reduce future likelihood/impact systematically. SP 800-53 less prescriptive on knowledge management from incidents.

clauses.title: Collection of evidence
clauses.rationale: AU-03 sets what audit records contain, which gives them value as evidence. AU-11 retains audit records long enough to support investigations of incidents after the fact. AU-10 provides irrefutable evidence of who performed an action, and through its enhancement AU-10(03) on chain of custody it keeps reviewer and releaser credentials within the chain of custody. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for evidence collection in incident handling and audit record review.
clauses.gaps: ISO focuses on digital forensics evidence handling for legal proceedings. The controls here cover the content, retention and non-repudiation of audit records. Procedures to identify, collect and preserve evidence after an incident fall outside this mapping.

clauses.title: Information security during disruption
clauses.rationale: The CP controls mapped here cover continuity planning and testing, alternate sites, backup and recovery. CP-13 adds alternative security mechanisms for when the primary ones are unavailable or compromised. Strong alignment.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: ICT readiness for business continuity
clauses.rationale: CP-02 sets the contingency plan, with essential functions, recovery objectives and restoration priorities. Through its enhancements CP-02(01) and CP-02(08), it coordinates that plan with related plans, such as business continuity plans, and identifies the critical assets behind essential functions. CP-04 tests the plan to check that it works and that the organization is ready to carry it out. CA-02 assesses whether controls are implemented correctly and work as intended. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for alternate processing and telecommunications, backup, system recovery and alternative security mechanisms.
clauses.gaps: ISO emphasizes ICT readiness specifically supporting business continuity plans. The controls here plan, test and assess that readiness. The capabilities that deliver it, such as alternate processing sites, backup and system recovery, fall outside this mapping.

clauses.title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
clauses.rationale: PM-01 sets the information security program plan. The policy controls mapped here, such as AC-01 and SR-01, require each policy to be consistent with applicable laws, regulations and standards. OSA lowered this figure from 60% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for contractual requirements and rules of behavior.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires explicit identification and documentation of all legal/regulatory/contractual requirements. SP 800-53 lacks a dedicated legal compliance identification control. FISMA context assumes federal requirements.

clauses.title: Intellectual property rights
clauses.rationale: No direct SP 800-53 control for intellectual property management.
clauses.gaps: Significant gap. SP 800-53 does not address software licensing, copyright compliance, or IP protection. Requires supplementary organizational controls.

clauses.title: Protection of records
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved access to records. AU-09 protects audit information from unauthorized change or deletion, and CP-09 backs information up. SC-08 and SC-28 protect confidentiality and integrity in transit and at rest. OSA lowered this figure from 70% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for the retention of records and audit logs.
clauses.gaps: ISO asks that records be kept safe from loss, tampering and unauthorized access, as legal and regulatory requirements demand. Retention periods and broader records management, such as classification and disposal schedules, fall outside this mapping.

clauses.title: Privacy and protection of PII
clauses.rationale: PM-18 sets the privacy program plan, and PT-01 a policy for processing PII in line with applicable laws. PT-03 limits processing to stated purposes and describes them in privacy notices. PT-07 sets conditions for specific categories of PII, and PL-02 adds privacy plans for systems. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for consent and the authority to process PII, among other privacy duties.
clauses.gaps: ISO defers to ISO 27701 for full privacy coverage. Consent and the authority to process PII fall outside this mapping.

clauses.title: Independent review of information security
clauses.rationale: CA-02 assesses the controls against a plan with a set scope and reports the results. Through its enhancement CA-02(01) on independent assessors, it has independent assessors or assessment teams carry out those assessments. OSA lowered this figure from 80% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for continuous monitoring and performance measures.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires independent review of the ISMS approach at planned intervals and after significant changes, beyond technical control assessment. CA-02 covers independent assessment of controls. Review of the management system as a whole is less explicit in SP 800-53.

clauses.title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards
clauses.rationale: CA-02 assesses compliance with security requirements, and CA-07 monitors control effectiveness on an ongoing basis. The policy controls mapped here, such as AC-01, require regular review of each policy and its procedures.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO requires regular review that information processing complies with policies. SP 800-53 assessment approach differs from compliance checking methodology.

clauses.title: Documented operating procedures
clauses.rationale: SA-05 provides administrator and user documentation, including how to configure and operate the system securely. The policy controls mapped here, such as CM-01 and MA-01, each require documented procedures for their family's controls.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires documented operating procedures for information processing facilities. SP 800-53 has family-specific procedures but no unified operating procedures control.

clauses.title: Screening
clauses.rationale: PS-03 directly covers personnel screening before access is granted.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Terms and conditions of employment
clauses.rationale: PS-06 covers access agreements that individuals sign before they get access. PL-04 sets rules of behavior that users acknowledge, describing their responsibilities for security and privacy. OSA lowered this figure from 88% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for security responsibilities in position descriptions.
clauses.gaps: ISO includes security responsibilities in employment contracts. The controls here cover access agreements and rules of behavior, which users sign or acknowledge. Security duties in position descriptions fall outside this mapping.

clauses.title: Information security awareness, education and training
clauses.rationale: AT-02 covers literacy training and awareness, and AT-03 role-based training. PM-13 sets up a security and privacy workforce program. CP-03 and IR-02 add training for contingency and incident response roles. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for training records and feedback on training.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. Training records and feedback on training results fall outside this mapping.

clauses.title: Disciplinary process
clauses.rationale: PS-08 covers personnel sanctions for security violations.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires formal disciplinary process communicated to employees. PS-08 addresses sanctions but formal process establishment less detailed.

clauses.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
clauses.rationale: PS-04 covers personnel termination; PS-05 covers personnel transfer. Both address ongoing responsibilities.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. PS-04/PS-05 address access revocation and ongoing obligations.

clauses.title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
clauses.rationale: PS-06 covers access agreements which include confidentiality requirements.
clauses.gaps: ISO specifically requires NDAs reflecting organizational needs. PS-06 is broader (access agreements) and NDA specifics are less detailed.

clauses.title: Remote working
clauses.rationale: AC-17 directly covers remote access controls. PE-17 covers alternate work sites.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO includes remote working security policies and risk considerations beyond technical access controls (physical environment, clean desk at home).

clauses.title: Information security event reporting
clauses.rationale: IR-06 directly covers incident reporting, with a set time for personnel to report suspected incidents. AU-06 reports findings from audit record review, and SI-02 covers reporting system flaws. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for incident response assistance.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Physical security perimeters
clauses.rationale: PE-03 covers physical access control, enforcing access at the facility's entry and exit points with access control devices or guards.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Physical entry
clauses.rationale: PE-02 physical access authorizations; PE-03 physical access control, which keeps access logs at entry points and escorts visitors. PE-16 controls the delivery and removal of system components. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for monitoring physical access and keeping visitor records.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. Comprehensive physical entry controls.

clauses.title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
clauses.rationale: PE-03 physical access control; PE-05 access control for output devices.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO includes broader facility security design considerations.

clauses.title: Physical security monitoring
clauses.rationale: PE-06 directly covers monitoring physical access. PE-03 keeps the physical access logs it reviews. AU-06, through its enhancement AU-06(06) on correlation with physical monitoring, ties audit records to physical access monitoring to spot unusual activity.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
clauses.rationale: PE controls cover the main environmental protections: power equipment (PE-09), fire (PE-13), temperature and humidity (PE-14) and water (PE-15). PE-23 (Facility Location) adds planning facility location considering physical and environmental hazards, directly addressing threat protection at the site selection level. PE-18 positions system components to limit damage from those hazards. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for emergency shutoff, emergency power and emergency lighting.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. PE-23 strengthens coverage by addressing hazard considerations in facility location planning.

clauses.title: Working in secure areas
clauses.rationale: NIST's crosswalk pairs no SP 800-53 control with this clause, so OSA maps none. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for physical access and visitor control in secure areas.
clauses.gaps: ISO includes rules for working in secure areas, such as no cameras and supervised work. The whole clause is a gap here.

clauses.title: Clear desk and clear screen
clauses.rationale: AC-11 covers session lock (clear screen). MP-04 covers media storage.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO explicitly addresses clear desk policy. AC-11 covers screen; desk policy is implied through MP controls but not explicitly stated.

clauses.title: Equipment siting and protection
clauses.rationale: PE-14 covers environmental controls; PE-18 location of components. PE-23 (Facility Location) addresses planning facility/site location considering physical and environmental hazards, supporting equipment siting decisions.
clauses.gaps: ISO includes equipment placement to minimize unauthorized access and environmental hazards. SP 800-53 less specific about equipment siting methodology but PE-23 adds site-level considerations.

clauses.title: Security of assets off-premises
clauses.rationale: MP-05 protects media in transport. AC-19 sets configuration and connection requirements for mobile devices, including outside controlled areas. PE-17 sets the controls for alternate work sites, and AC-20 sets the terms for using external systems. OSA lowered this figure from 80% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for remote access and the protection of stored information.
clauses.gaps: ISO covers all off-premises assets (laptops, paper, etc.). SP 800-53 covers media and mobile devices but physical asset protection off-site less comprehensive.

clauses.title: Storage media
clauses.rationale: The MP family covers media protection: access (MP-02), storage (MP-04), transport (MP-05), sanitization (MP-06), use (MP-07). PE-16 controls media and other components entering and leaving the facility, and MA-02 sanitizes media before equipment leaves for off-site maintenance. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for media policy, media marking and media downgrading.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Supporting utilities
clauses.rationale: PE-09 power equipment protection; PE-10 emergency shutoff; PE-11 emergency power; PE-12 emergency lighting.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Cabling security
clauses.rationale: PE-04 covers access control for transmission medium. PE-09 covers power equipment/cabling protection. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it set one figure for this control and its twin in ISO/IEC 27002:2022, which has the same controls.
clauses.gaps: ISO includes specific cabling security measures, such as protected routing and shielding. PE-04 is more general.

clauses.title: Equipment maintenance
clauses.rationale: MA-02 covers controlled maintenance: it schedules, approves and monitors all maintenance, on site or remote, and checks the controls afterwards. MA-06 gets maintenance support and spare parts within a set time of a failure. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for maintenance policy, maintenance tools and personnel, and remote and field maintenance.
clauses.gaps: Minor: maintenance personnel, maintenance tools and remote maintenance rest on MA-02's general approval and monitoring of maintenance.

clauses.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
clauses.rationale: MP-06 covers media sanitization before disposal, release or re-use. OSA lowered this figure from 92% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for media use and assessing equipment for re-use.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO includes all equipment disposal, while SP 800-53 focuses on media.

clauses.title: User endpoint devices
clauses.rationale: AC-19 sets configuration and connection requirements for mobile devices such as phones and tablets. AC-11 locks any device after inactivity until the user signs in again. OSA lowered this figure from 80% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for least functionality and the encryption of stored information.
clauses.gaps: ISO covers all user endpoint devices holistically (BYOD, MDM, containerization). AC-19 covers mobile devices such as phones and tablets, so laptops and desktops rest on AC-11 alone. Endpoint hardening and storage encryption are uncovered.

clauses.title: Privileged access rights
clauses.rationale: AC-06 directly covers least privilege including privileged access restriction, review, and authorization. Comprehensive coverage.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Information access restriction
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved authorizations for logical access. AC-24 applies access control decisions to each access request before enforcement. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for information flow control and least privilege.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Access to source code
clauses.rationale: CM-05 covers access restrictions for change, including software libraries; AC-03 access enforcement. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for developer configuration management of source code.
clauses.gaps: ISO specifically addresses source code access restrictions. Here they rest on access restrictions for change and access enforcement. Version control of the source code repository is uncovered.

clauses.title: Secure authentication
clauses.rationale: AC-07 limits unsuccessful logon attempts, AC-08 shows a notice before logon, AC-09 reports the last logon, and IA-06 obscures authentication feedback. Together they cover a secure logon procedure. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for identifying and authenticating users, managing authenticators and re-authentication.
clauses.gaps: The controls here cover the logon procedure. The authentication mechanism itself, such as multi-factor authentication suited to the information's sensitivity, is uncovered.

clauses.title: Capacity management
clauses.rationale: CP-02, through its enhancement CP-02(02) on capacity planning, plans for the processing, telecommunications and environmental capacity needed during contingency operations. SC-05, through its enhancement SC-05(02), manages capacity, bandwidth and redundancy to limit the effects of flooding attacks. AU-04 allocates audit log storage capacity. OSA lowered this figure from 72% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for resource availability.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires proactive capacity management for all IT resources, with monitoring and forecasting. The controls here cover capacity for contingency operations, resilience to denial of service and audit log storage. Day-to-day monitoring and forecasting of capacity fall outside this mapping.

clauses.title: Protection against malware
clauses.rationale: SI-03 directly covers malicious code protection. AT-02 builds the user awareness the clause also asks for.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
clauses.rationale: RA-05 vulnerability monitoring and scanning; SI-02 flaw remediation; SI-05 security alerts.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Configuration management
clauses.rationale: The CM family covers configuration management: policy (CM-01), baselines (CM-02), change control (CM-03), impact analysis (CM-04), access restrictions (CM-05), settings (CM-06), inventory (CM-08) and the configuration management plan (CM-09). SA-10 extends configuration management to the system's developers. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for least functionality, software usage restrictions, user-installed software and signed components.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Information deletion
clauses.rationale: MP-06 sanitizes media before disposal, release or reuse. SI-21 deletes information when it's no longer needed, and MA-02 sanitizes equipment before it leaves for off-site maintenance. MP-04 protects media until they are sanitized or destroyed. NIST also names enhancements that sanitize in particular cases. AC-04, through AC-04(25), sanitizes data that moves between security domains. AC-07, through AC-07(02), wipes a mobile device after repeated failed logons. MA-03, through MA-03(03), and MA-04, through MA-04(03), sanitize equipment and components used in maintenance. OSA lowered this figure from 80% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for information retention and component disposal.
clauses.gaps: ISO specifically addresses information deletion when no longer required. SP 800-53 covers sanitization, and SI-21 deletes refreshed information when it's no longer needed. Retention schedules are uncovered here.

clauses.title: Data masking
clauses.rationale: SI-19 removes chosen elements of personally identifiable information from datasets and checks that de-identification works. Through its enhancement SI-19(04), it removes, masks, encrypts, hashes or replaces direct identifiers. AC-04, through its enhancement AC-04(23), modifies information that may not be released when it moves between security domains. OSA lowered this figure from 80% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for the handling of personal data.
clauses.gaps: ISO specifically addresses data masking techniques, such as pseudonymization, anonymization and masking. SI-19 applies them to personal data. Masking other sensitive data, in line with access policy, is less explicit.

clauses.title: Data leakage prevention
clauses.rationale: SC-07, through its enhancement SC-07(10) on preventing exfiltration, stops information leaving through the system boundary and tests for exfiltration. PE-03, through its enhancement PE-03(02), checks the physical perimeter for information or components being taken out. SI-20 embeds data or capabilities that reveal exfiltration, and AU-13 monitors open sources for signs that information has been disclosed. PE-19 protects against leakage through electromagnetic emanations. OSA lowered this figure from 80% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for information flow enforcement and system monitoring.
clauses.gaps: ISO specifically addresses DLP. The controls here block and detect exfiltration at the boundary, at the perimeter and in open sources. Rules that decide which data may flow where, and monitoring of endpoints and email, fall outside this mapping.

clauses.title: Information backup
clauses.rationale: CP-09 directly covers information system backup. It sets how often to back up user and system information, in line with recovery objectives, and protects the backups. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for alternate storage sites for backups.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
clauses.rationale: CP-06 sets up an alternate storage site and CP-07 an alternate processing site. CP-02 sets the contingency plan that these sites serve. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for alternate telecommunications services.
clauses.gaps: ISO focuses on redundancy for availability. CP controls focus on contingency, which includes redundancy. Redundant telecommunications links are now a gap.

clauses.title: Logging
clauses.rationale: AU controls cover logging: the events to log (AU-02), record content (AU-03), review and analysis (AU-06), protection (AU-09), retention (AU-11), record generation (AU-12) and session audit (AU-14). OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for logging policy, log storage capacity, logging failures, report generation, time stamps and non-repudiation.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Monitoring activities
clauses.rationale: SI-04 directly covers system monitoring. IR-04, through its enhancement IR-04(13) on behavior analysis, analyzes anomalous or suspected adversarial behavior. AC-02, through AC-02(12), monitors accounts for atypical use. AC-17, through AC-17(01), monitors and controls remote access, and MA-04, through MA-04(01), logs and reviews remote maintenance sessions. SC-07 monitors communications at the system boundary, PE-06 monitors physical access, and AU-13 watches for disclosure of organizational information. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for audit record review and continuous monitoring.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Clock synchronization
clauses.rationale: AU-08 time stamps audit records from the system's internal clocks, in UTC or with a stated offset. The organization sets how closely those clocks must match reference clocks. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it set one figure for this control and its twin in ISO/IEC 27002:2022, which has the same controls.
clauses.gaps: Synchronizing clocks to approved time sources, the core of this clause, is a gap here. AU-08 covers the time stamps themselves.

clauses.title: Use of privileged utility programs
clauses.rationale: AC-06 applies least privilege, so only authorized users can reach privileged utilities. AC-03 enforces approved authorizations for access. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for restricting unneeded programs and user-installed software.
clauses.gaps: ISO specifically addresses privileged utility programs. SP 800-53 addresses them through general access controls. Removing or disabling utilities that aren't needed is now a gap.

clauses.title: Installation of software on operational systems
clauses.rationale: CM-05 restricts access for changes, including software installation. CM-07 applies least functionality. CM-11 governs user-installed software. OSA lowered this figure from 92% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for signed components and unsupported system components.
clauses.gaps: Small gaps remain: verifying software signatures before installation, and keeping installed software at a supported version.

clauses.title: Networks security
clauses.rationale: SC-07 protects the boundary and SC-08 protects transmissions. AC-18 governs wireless access, AC-20 the use of external systems, and SC-10 ends network connections after a session or a period of inactivity. AC-03 enforces approved access. OSA lowered this figure from 92% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for information flow enforcement and internal system connections.
clauses.gaps: Small gaps remain: controlling information flows within the network, and authorizing and documenting internal system connections.

clauses.title: Security of network services
clauses.rationale: SA-09 requires providers of external services, including network services, to meet security requirements, and monitors their compliance. CA-03 approves and manages information exchanges through agreements, such as service level agreements, that document security requirements. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for boundary protection and transmission confidentiality and integrity.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires security features, service levels and management requirements for network services. Service level specifics are less detailed in SP 800-53. The technical protection of the services themselves, such as boundary protection and encryption in transit, is now a gap.

clauses.title: Segregation of networks
clauses.rationale: SC-07 boundary protection with segmentation. AC-04 controls information flows between segments. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for system partitioning.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Web filtering
clauses.rationale: SC-07 monitors and controls communications at the boundary, where web filtering takes place. AC-04 enforces information flow policies, such as limiting web requests to those that pass through an approved proxy. OSA lowered this figure from 75% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for malicious code protection.
clauses.gaps: ISO specifically addresses web filtering. SP 800-53 doesn't have a dedicated web filtering control; addressed through general boundary and content controls.

clauses.title: Use of cryptography
clauses.rationale: SC-12 cryptographic key management; SC-13 cryptographic protection; SC-17 public key infrastructure certificates.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 cryptography controls are comprehensive.

clauses.title: Secure development life cycle
clauses.rationale: SA-03 system development life cycle; SA-15 development process, standards and tools; SA-17 developer security architecture and design. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for security engineering principles, developer configuration management and developer testing.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 SA family is comprehensive for secure development.

clauses.title: Application security requirements
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved access authorizations. SC-08 protects information in transit, and SC-13 sets the cryptography to use. These cover security functions that application requirements commonly specify. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for security requirements in acquisitions and security engineering principles.
clauses.gaps: The controls here cover specific security functions. Identifying, specifying and approving an application's security requirements during development or acquisition is now a gap.

clauses.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
clauses.rationale: SA-08 security engineering principles; SA-17 developer security architecture.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Secure coding
clauses.rationale: SA-15 has developers follow a documented development process with set standards and tools, and through its enhancement SA-15(05) reduce attack surfaces. SA-11 requires developer testing and flaw remediation, and through SA-11(01) static code analysis. SA-04, through SA-04(03), requires developers to show the development methods and practices they use. SA-08 applies security and privacy engineering principles, and SA-10 manages changes to source code under configuration management. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for developer training and security architecture.
clauses.gaps: ISO specifically addresses secure coding practices. The controls here set the development process, its standards, static analysis and testing. Training developers in secure coding falls outside this mapping.

clauses.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
clauses.rationale: SA-11 directly covers developer security testing. CA-02 security assessments. SA-04 includes testing requirements. SR-05, through its enhancement SR-05(02), assesses a system, component or service before it is selected, accepted, modified or updated.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Outsourced development
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition requirements; SA-10/SA-11 developer requirements apply to outsourced development. SA-15 has the developer follow a documented process that the organization reviews. SR-02 and SR-04 add supply chain risk planning and provenance.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO specifically addresses outsourced development supervision and acceptance. SP 800-53 covers through general acquisition controls.

clauses.title: Separation of development, test and production environments
clauses.rationale: CM-04, through its enhancement CM-04(01) on separate test environments, analyzes changes in a separate test environment before they reach the operational one. CM-05 limits who can make changes to the system, through access restrictions, software libraries and change windows. SA-03 manages the system through a development life cycle that builds in security. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for developer testing and system partitioning.
clauses.gaps: ISO explicitly requires environment separation. The controls here keep testing apart from production and restrict who changes production. Keeping development apart from both is less explicit.

clauses.title: Change management
clauses.rationale: CM-03 configuration change control, with approval that weighs security impact; CM-05 access restrictions for change; SA-10 developer configuration management. SI-02 tests flaw remediation updates before installation. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for security impact analysis.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Test information
clauses.rationale: SA-03 manages the system through a development life cycle that builds in security. Through its enhancement SA-03(02) on the use of live or operational data, it approves, documents and controls the use of live data in preproduction environments, and protects those environments at the level of the live data. OSA lowered this figure from 70% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for developer testing and development process standards.
clauses.gaps: ISO specifically addresses the protection of test data, such as anonymizing it and controlling the use of production data in testing. SA-03 controls the use of live data in testing. Choosing and anonymizing test data are less explicit.

clauses.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
clauses.rationale: NIST's crosswalk pairs no SP 800-53 control with this clause, so OSA maps none. OSA lowered this figure from 78% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for control assessments, audit record review and penetration testing.
clauses.gaps: ISO requires that audit testing be planned and agreed to keep business disruption low. With no control mapped, the whole clause is a gap.
